newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway shares hit new all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Norway shares hit new all-time high.

text.p: The Oslo Bourse soared to new peaks on Friday, joining the rally at major European stock exchanges following an overnight all-time high on Wall Street.
Dealers said the Norwegian market was also inspired by good liquidity and strong annual company results this week.

The Total index closed 0.91 percent up at 1,094.44 for a record close after hitting an intraday high at 1,107.65 points. Turnover was heavy at 1.3 billion crowns. Gains were recorded across the board, except in the shipping index, which fell.
The winner of the day was food-based conglomerate Orkla , whose pre-tax profits jumped 29 percent.
Orkla's A share finished 28.50 crowns, or 5.60 percent, higher at 537 crowns in healthy trade worth 96 million crowns.

The company said it was taking over the 52-percent stake held by Swedish carmaker AB Volvo in jointly-owned beverages company Pripps-Ringnes as part of a strategy to grow its business in eastern Europe.

"This takeover sounds very good," one analyst said. "Orkla may form joint ventures with other companies, perhaps already this year. This a confirmation of what Orkla has done for 50 years, namely investing in areas where there is still structural profit to be had."
